analysis: Reviewed the two supplied base_text units of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (lines 9140-10756). The visible patch excerpt shows only prompt_contract_id hex string replacements for the Qwen model (6bb9fb05... -> 8171fec3...). Changed ranges in the Gemma and Qwen sections (e.g. 9229, 9310, 9375, 9499, 9579, 9631, 9704, 9934, 10096, 10161, 10471) are single-line changes consistent with prompt_contract_id updates; these are the only changed lines in the supplied units. This is a test-fixture file (golden vectors), not executable code, auth logic, or key material. The fixture content contains no secrets: it holds synthetic prompts, token IDs and a fixture scope. No change to the coordinator to provider WebSocket contract (TB-002), attestation (TB-009), App Attest authorization (TB-011) or encryption paths is visible. The base text is shown only; head text for the new IDs was not supplied, so I could not verify that Gemma contract IDs and the token vectors changed consistently. Security relevance is limited to cache routing eligibility (cache_routing_eligible true, T-041): the prompt_contract_id presumably scopes prefix-cache sharing, so a changed contract id should invalidate old cache artifacts. That depends on the unseen Swift/Go code that computes the id, which is not in this batch. Remaining integration question: whether the prompt-contract hash derivation change (source files not supplied here) is consistent between coordinator and provider and whether it keeps cache isolation properties; this is a fixture-only view, so no finding is raised.
